title: Calls, texts & voice notes
goal: Answer and make calls, cope with a bad line, apologise for a missed call, message and voice-note friends, share your location, and say what you have just, already, or still not done.
intro:
Nepalis live on their phones: calls to family, voice messages to friends, group chats for everything. This unit gives you the phone Nepali you'll need every day — **हेलो, को बोल्नुभएको?**, **मेरो आवाज सुनिन्छ?**, **तिम्रो मिस कल देखेँ**, **लोकेसन पठाइदेऊ न** — and the English words (कल, म्यासेज, ब्याट्री, नेट) with the Nepali verbs that go with them.

The grammar is about sequence and timing: 'do X and then Y' (**-एर**, **-एपछि**, **-नुअघि**, **नगरी**) and 'just / already / still / not yet' (**भर्खरै**, **-इसक्नु**, **अझै**, **अहिलेसम्म**, **बाँकी**). You'll also meet the short spoken forms people use in chat: **के गर्दै?**, **कहाँ गएको?**, **भन्नुस् न**.

grammar.title: Do X and then Y: -एर, -एपछि, -नुअघि, नगरी
grammar.body:
You met **-एर** in unit 20: म घर **पुगेर** म्यासेज गर्छु 'I'll get home and (then) text you'. Here is the full family of 'sequence' forms:

**-एर** 'having done → and then'. Normally the **same person** does both actions. It can also give a **reason**: नेट **नभएर** पठाउन सकिनँ 'I couldn't send it because there was no internet'. With **पनि** it means 'even though / despite': म्यासेज **हेरेर पनि** रिप्लाई गरेन 'he saw the message but still didn't reply'.

**-एपछि** 'after (doing)'. Use it when the two actions have **different** subjects, or to stress the order: तिमी **पुगेपछि** मलाई कल गर 'call me after you get there'. Vowel stems: आएपछि, खाएपछि; जानु → **गएपछि**, हुनु → **भएपछि**.

**-नुअघि** 'before (doing)': the dictionary form + अघि: **निस्कनुअघि** 'before leaving', **सुत्नुअघि** 'before going to sleep'.

**नगरी** 'without doing': न- + stem + **-ई**: **नभनी** 'without saying', **नखाई** 'without eating', **नसोधी** 'without asking'. Speech often adds -कन: नभनीकन.

The trap: don't use -एर when the doers differ — say तिमी **आएपछि** हामी खान्छौँ 'we'll eat after you come', not तिमी आएर हामी खान्छौँ.

examples.en: He saw the message but still didn't reply.

grammar.title: Just, already, still, not yet
grammar.body:
Four little tools for timing:

**भर्खर / भर्खरै** 'just (now)' with the simple past: म **भर्खरै** उठेँ 'I've only just woken up', उसले **भर्खर** म्यासेज पठायो 'he just sent a message'.

**-इसक्नु** 'already' (unit 17): stem + **-इ** + सक्नु: मैले **पठाइसकेँ** 'I've already sent it', ऊ **गइसक्यो** 'he's already gone'. As a question it means 'yet?': **पढिसक्यौ?** 'have you read it yet?'.

**अझै** 'still' with a positive verb, 'still not / not yet' with a negative: ऊ **अझै** अनलाइन छ 'he's still online', बस **अझै** आएन 'the bus still hasn't come'. **अहिलेसम्म** 'up to now' + the negative perfect **-एको छैन** is the clearest 'not yet': **अहिलेसम्म** रिप्लाई **गरेको छैन** 'hasn't replied yet'.

**-न बाँकी छ** 'is still to be done' — very natural Nepali for 'I haven't … yet': मेरो खाना खान **बाँकी छ** 'I haven't eaten yet', दुईवटा कल गर्न **बाँकी छ** 'two calls still to make'.

A quick answer to 'have you done it?': **गरिसकेँ** 'done already', **अझै छैन** 'not yet', **भर्खरै गरेँ** 'just did'.

examples.native: मेरो अझै दुईवटा कल गर्न बाँकी छ।
examples.roman: mero ajhai duiwaṭā kal garna bāṃki chha.
examples.en: I've still got two calls to make.

grammar.title: Short spoken forms: -नुस्, -एको?, -दै?
grammar.body:
Phone calls and chats use clipped forms that you'll hear far more than the textbook ones:

**-नुस्** is the everyday spoken version of the polite command **-नुहोस्**: **भन्नुस्** 'go ahead, say it', **बस्नुस्** 'have a seat', **पर्खनुस्** 'please wait'. It's still polite (तपाईं level) — just relaxed. Writing usually keeps the full -नुहोस्.

**-एको?** as a whole question, with छ/हो dropped, asks about something done: **कहाँ गएको?** 'where did you go / where have you been?', **किन नउठाएको?** 'why didn't you pick up?', **को बोल्नुभएको?** 'who's speaking?' (polite). It works for any person, so it's handy.

**-दै?** alone asks what someone's doing right now: **के गर्दै?** 'what are you up to?' (= के गर्दै छौ?). Typical opening of a chat.

On the phone you also say **म [name] बोलेको** 'this is [name] speaking', and answer elders and strangers with **हजुर** 'yes?'. In chats young people type Nepali in Roman letters — *k xa?* (के छ?), *huss* (हस्), *ma aaudai xu* — where **x** stands for छ.

dialogue.title: A bad line to Pokhara
dialogue.setting: Sabin is on a tourist bus to Pokhara. His friend Priya finally gets through to him.

lines.speaker: Sabin
lines.en: Hi Priya! Can you hear me?

lines.speaker: Priya
lines.native: अलिअलि सुनिन्छ। कहाँ छौ? हिजो किन फोन नउठाएको?
lines.roman: aliali suninchha. kahāṃ chhau? hijo kina phon nauṭhāeko?
lines.en: Sort of. Where are you? Why didn't you pick up yesterday?

lines.speaker: Sabin
lines.native: सरी, फोन अफ थियो। अहिले बसमा पोखरा जाँदै छु।
lines.roman: sari, phon aph thiyo. ahile basmā Pokharā jāṃdai chhu.
lines.en: Sorry, my phone was off. I'm on the bus to Pokhara right now.

lines.speaker: Priya
lines.en: What did you say? I can't hear you properly.

lines.speaker: Sabin
lines.en: On the bus! The signal's bad around Mugling.

lines.speaker: Priya
lines.native: ठीक छ। पोखरा पुगेपछि म्यासेज गर न।
lines.roman: ṭhik chha. Pokharā pugepachhi myāsej gara na.
lines.en: OK. Text me once you get to Pokhara.

lines.speaker: Sabin
lines.native: हुन्छ। अनि सुन, तिम्रो दिदीको नम्बर म्यासेन्जरमा पठाइदेऊ न। मैले सेभ गरेको छैन।
lines.roman: hunchha. ani suna, timro didiko nambar myāsenjarmā paṭhāideu na. maile sebh gareko chhaina.
lines.en: Will do. And listen, send me your sister's number on Messenger, will you? I haven't saved it.

lines.speaker: Priya
lines.en: Just sent it. Have a look.

lines.speaker: Sabin
lines.native: अँ, आयो, थ्याङ्क्यु! ल, मेरो ब्याट्री सकिन लाग्यो।
lines.roman: aṃ, āyo, thyāṅkyu! la, mero byāṭri sakina lāgyo.
lines.en: Yep, got it, thanks! Right, my battery's about to die.

lines.speaker: Priya
lines.native: फेरि? तिम्रो फोनमा कहिल्यै चार्ज हुँदैन!
lines.roman: pheri? timro phonmā kahilyai chārj huṃdaina!
lines.en: Again? Your phone is never charged!

lines.speaker: Sabin
lines.native: हाहा, पुगेर चार्ज गर्छु। भ्वाइस म्यासेज पठाउँछु है। फोन राख्छु!
lines.roman: hāhā, pugera chārj garchhu. bhwāis myāsej paṭhāuṃchhu hai. phon rākhchhu!
lines.en: Haha, I'll charge it when I get there. I'll send you a voice message. Bye for now!

culture: Nepalis answer the phone with **हेलो** — and, to an older or unknown caller, **हजुर?** Calls usually start with **के छ?** or **खाना खानुभयो?** ('have you eaten?') before getting to the point, and end with **फोन राख्छु है** rather than a formal goodbye. With older relatives, call rather than text. Among friends, voice messages on **Messenger** and **Viber** are hugely popular (typing Devanagari on a phone is slow), and when people do type they mostly use Roman letters: *k xa?*, *thik xa*, *aaudai xu* — the **x** is छ. A deliberate **मिस कल** used to mean 'call me back' when credit was short, and older people still do it. Millions of Nepalis work in the Gulf, Malaysia and Korea, so the evening **भिडियो कल** home is part of family life, and a bad line ('**आवाज आएन!**') is something everyone knows. With colleagues and elders use **तपाईं** and the relaxed polite **-नुस्** (भन्नुस्, पर्खनुस्); with friends, तिमी.

tip.title: On the phone: -नुस् and -एको?
tip.body:
- **-नुस्** is spoken **-नुहोस्**: **भन्नुस्** 'go ahead', **पर्खनुस्** 'please wait' — still polite.
- Say who you are with **बोलेको**: म सबिन **बोलेको**.
- A bare **-एको?** asks about something done: कहाँ **गएको**? 'where did you go?'
- Answer elders with **हजुर?**
tip.pattern: म + name + बोलेको  ·  भन्नुस्  ·  कहाँ गएको?

tip.title: Just, already, still, not yet
tip.body:
- **भर्खरै** + past = 'just': भर्खरै देखेँ.
- **-इसक्नु** = 'already': पठा**इसकेँ**; as a question 'yet?': पढ**िसक्यौ**?
- **अझै** = 'still'; with a negative 'not yet': अझै पढेको छैन.
- **-न बाँकी छ** = 'still to do': खान **बाँकी छ**.

sentences.en: I've only just seen your message.
He hasn't answered yet.
My sister is still online.

sentences.native: मैले तिमीलाई तीनवटा मिस कल दिइसकेँ!
sentences.roman: maile timilāi tinwaṭā mis kal diisakeṃ!
sentences.en: I've already given you three missed calls!
Have you read the message yet?
Haven't read it yet, I'll look later.

sentences.native: मेरो अझै खाना खान बाँकी छ।
sentences.roman: mero ajhai khānā khāna bāṃki chha.
sentences.en: I still haven't eaten.
Sorry, I've just woken up.

sentences.native: किन रिप्लाई नगरेको? म कुरिरहेको थिएँ।
sentences.roman: kina riplāi nagareko? ma kuriraheko thieṃ.
sentences.en: Why didn't you reply? I was waiting.
I forgot to reply, sorry.

lessons.title: Voice notes, video calls and groups

tip.title: English noun + गर्नु
tip.body:
- Most phone words are English nouns + **गर्नु**: कल **गर्नु**, म्यासेज **गर्नु**, टाइप **गर्नु**, सेभ **गर्नु**, रिप्लाई **गर्नु**.
- 'Send' is **पठाउनु**: भ्वाइस म्यासेज **पठाउनु**.
- A missed call is *given*: मिस कल **दिनु**.

sentences.native: टाइप गर्ने समय छैन, भ्वाइस म्यासेज पठाउँछु।
sentences.roman: ṭāip garne samaya chhaina, bhwāis myāsej paṭhāuṃchhu.

sentences.roman: āja belukā bhiḍiyo kal garauṃ na.
sentences.en: Let's video call this evening.
I'll add you to the group.
Message everyone in the group.
Send me a voice message on Messenger.

sentences.roman: maile mis kal dieṃ, usle kal garchha.
sentences.en: I gave him a missed call — he'll ring back.

tip.title: Before, after, without
tip.body:
- **-एर** = 'and then' (same person) or 'because': नेट **नभएर** पठाउन सकिनँ.
- **-एपछि** = 'after': घर **पुगेपछि** चार्ज गर्छु.
- **-नुअघि** = 'before': **निस्कनुअघि** फोन गर.
- **न- … -ई** = 'without': मलाई **नभनी** 'without telling me'.

sentences.en: I'll charge my phone after I get home.
Send me the location before you leave.
The battery died and the phone switched off.
I couldn't send the message because there was no internet.
I'll follow the location and find my way.
